Chapter 2 Q1. What type of data is it? Describe it

Chapter 2 Q1. What type of data is it? Describe it vect2sql <- function(x){ paste("('", paste(x, collapse = "','"), "')", sep = "") } gse_ids <- c("GSE201427","GSE166530","GSE162183","GSE186458") gse_sql <- vect2sql(gse_ids) # dbListTables(con) # dbListFields(con, 'gpl') sql <- paste( "SELECT DISTINCT gse_gpl.gse, gse_gpl.gpl, gse.title", "FROM gse JOIN gse_gpl ON gse_gpl.gse = gse.gse", "WHERE gse.gse IN", gse_sql, sep = " ") series <- dbGetQuery(con, sql) GSE186458, GSE166530, GSE162183: Illumina NovaSeq 6000 (Homo sapiens), high-throughput sequencing (RNA-seq) GSE201427: Illumina HiSeq 4000 (Homo sapiens), high-throughput sequencing (RNA-seq)

Chapter 3 Q2. What disease or model is it using?

Chapter 3 Q2. What disease or model is it using? sql <- paste( "SELECT DISTINCT gse, overall_design, variable, variable_description, pubmed_id, summary", "FROM gse", "WHERE gse IN", gse_sql, sep = " ") model <- dbGetQuery(con, sql) GSE162183: Single cell RNA-seq study of human psoriasis skin. GSE166530: Differential expression analysis of RNA-Seq data from COVID-19 positive samples against COVID-19 negative control. GSE186458: Genome-wide patterns of DNA methylation across a variety of cell types in healthy adults. GSE201427: Panc1 cells were treated either with control siRNA (siCtrl) or siRNA targeting SF3B1 (siSF3B1). siCtrl cells were exposed to 1% O2 or 21% O2, siSF3B1 cells to 1% O2 for 8 hours. 1% O2 mimics hypoxia.

q5.-can-you-find-out-any-information-about-the-geo-dataset---gse264108.-why-or-why-not.html
Chapter 6 Q5. Can you find out any information about the GEO dataset - GSE264108. Why or Why not?

Chapter 6 Q5. Can you find out any information about the GEO dataset - GSE264108. Why or Why not? sql <- paste( "SELECT DISTINCT *", "FROM gse", "WHERE gse LIKE '%GSE264108%'", sep = " ") dbGetQuery(con, sql) ## [1] ID title gse ## [4] status submission_date last_update_date ## [7] pubmed_id summary type ## [10] contributor web_link overall_design ## [13] repeats repeats_sample_list variable ## [16] variable_description contact supplementary_file ## <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names) sql <- paste( "SELECT DISTINCT *", "FROM gse_gpl", "WHERE gse LIKE '%GSE264108%'", sep = " ") dbGetQuery(con, sql) ## [1] gse gpl ## <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names) sql <- "SELECT submission_date FROM gse" dates <- dbGetQuery(con, sql) max(dates[[1]]) ## [1] "2024-02-29" None of the tables have GSE264108 in them. This is because this GSE became public on Jan 25, 2025, but the oldest GSE in the database is from Feb 29, 2024. This gets at the issue with this method of querying GEO as we rely on a static instance of the database that may be almost 2 years out of date.
